newsitem.title: GERMANY: Viag /BT add Telenor, seek new partner.
newsitem.headline: Viag /BT add Telenor, seek new partner.

text.p: German diversified utilities group Viag AG and British Telecom said on Thursday they had added a new partner to their joint activities, Norway's Telenor, and were seeking a further partner.
The two companies said at a joint news conference that Telnor was taking a 10 percent stake in their joint operations.

Viag management board chairman Georg Obermeier described Telenor as a "technical partner" and said the companies were seeking a partner with expertise in direct sales to take a 10 percent stake in the new VIAG Interkom. They were in talks with some companies, but there was no agreement yet, he said.

Obermeier also said that VIAG and BT expected sales in their joint telecoms activities to reach up to 11 billion marks ($6.7 billion) in 1997. The activities would break even in 2002, the two companies predicted.
Viag and BT were awarded Germany's fourth mobile phone licence E2 earlier this week.

The companies said they planned to invest about seven billion marks in creating a integrated fixed and mobile network by 2007 and hoped to secure around eight percent of the overall German telecommunications market.
